chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil told us, saying: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi told us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Rabi' al-Warraq, from Salih ibn Sahl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Everything is to perish, except for His Face.' He said: We.
ai.seo_question: Who does 'His Face' refer to in the verse 'Everything is to perish, except for His Face'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets 'His Face' in Surah al-Qasas as referring to the Imams, thereby establishing their ontological permanence amidst the transience of creation. This interpretation underscores the Shia doctrine of *Tawhid al-Af'ali* and the Imams' role as the enduring locus of divine authority and worship. It highlights the theological significance of the Ahl al-Bayt as the eternal manifestation of God's will on earth.
